newsitem.title: USA: Hunt still on for Oklahoma bond adviser.
newsitem.headline: Hunt still on for Oklahoma bond adviser.

text.p: The committee charged with selecting a replacement for Oklahoma State Bond Advisor James Joseph is tentatively scheduled to meet next week after postponing Tuesday's meeting.

"The selection committee was supposed to meet yesterday to short list the names that they would like to interview, but there was a conflict with legislative schedules so it was postponed," Joseph said Wednesday.
In January, Joseph announced that he would leave the post he has held since September 1991 to become a partner at Government Finance Group Inc, an Arlington, Va., financial advisory firm.
Since April 1, Joseph has been dividing his time between Oklahoma and his new firm, and hopes to join the Government Finance Group fulltime by June 1.

While ideally Joseph would like to leave the Oklahoma post as soon as a replacement can be found, he will stay on through the end of Oklahoma's current legislative session, which ends in late May, he said.

The selection committee includes two members each from the Executive Bond Oversight Commission and the Legislative Bond Oversight Commission. They are: Oklahoma Department of Commerce Executive Director Leo Presley; Lieutenant Governor Mary Fallin; Sen. Ted Fisher, (D-12); and Rep. Ron Langmacher, (D-56).
